Parents who choose Priyanshvansh usually hope their child will grow to embody loved by shiva and live with faith, good character and purpose.

historical_references.reference: The Priyavrata dynasty, to which Priyanshvansh belongs, is believed to be the second of the seven Prajapati dynasties in Hindu mythology. It is said that the first king of the Priyavrata dynasty was the sage Priyavrata, who was the son of the god Brahma and obtained the entire earth as his kingdom. Priyanshvansh is believed to be a descendant of this sage-king and is mentioned in various Hindu texts, including the Mahabharata and the Puranas.

Another reference to Priyanshvansh can be found in the Mahabharata, specifically in the Anushasana Parva (Book of Instructions), where he is mentioned as a great king who ruled over the earth and was renowned for his wisdom, justice, and righteousness. He is said to have had a debate with Yudhishthira, the eldest of the Pandava brothers, on the topic of dharma (duty or moral virtue) and is revered as a sage and a model of righteous rule.
